scope: Reviewable plan, not runtime configuration. Five playable stages exist. Later entries are proposals unless marked user-direction; that status approves the direction, not its implementation.
inheritance: Keep earlier capacities available. Each encounter foregrounds one new operation; bounded modules and quiet areas prevent every accumulated effect running everywhere. Object IDs, seed, coordinate frame and state ownership must be explicit.

stages.title: Primitives
stages.operation: Form shelters a body.
stages.world: White ground, thin black outlines, six tall shelters and a clear route. Static heads stand on poles.
stages.catalyst: The carried sphere and hand form fire small balls. A ladder skull falls after one hit.
stages.counterpart: Slow straight shots; the player can step behind a solid form.
stages.reuse: Keep the current cover and hit path. Earlier biome_primitives records offer stable identities for a later bridge into the habitat.
stages.next_work: Retest the B16 skull fix in the headset; retain one-hit ladder defeat and three-hit player health.
stages.acceptance: A real shot defeats a visible skull in READY, PLAY and REST; the skull physically falls. Cover blocks an incoming shot; the open lane does not.
changes: Check in VR that a hit skull falls and cover blocks its shots.
Temporary editor persistence check.

stages.title: Transformation
stages.operation: The same form moves, turns and scales.
stages.world: Keep the fixed entrance refuge; other cover translates, rotates or grows from the ground. Pickups remain reachable.
stages.catalyst: A tile hit multiplies scale by 0.8 and turns it 22.5 degrees around Y.
stages.counterpart: Heads move and turn; their slow balls grow within a fixed bound.
stages.reuse: Current motion records and collision-following bodies; rising_banners shows how the very same panels can retain identity through transforms.
stages.next_work: Make each operation readable in play with a short label or motion cue, while leaving the refuge fixed.
stages.acceptance: Sample moving cover over a full cycle: refuge, collision and route remain usable; tile impacts retain their measured scale and turn.
changes: Make moving, rotating and scaling cover easier to read. Keep the entrance refuge still.

stages.title: Arrays
stages.operation: A slot remains when its occupant falls.
stages.world: Black-and-white addressed floor; three indexed heads, with inherited transformations and cover.
stages.catalyst: Choose one occupant; preserve the other slots and all earlier tile responses.
stages.counterpart: A small ordered row; a defeated head leaves a legible vacancy.
stages.reuse: The current row and tile address arrays. Keep indices independent of world position and live body references.
stages.next_work: Expose the row from arrival: Claude's capture review found the cylinders hide it and the labels are too far away.
stages.acceptance: Removing the middle occupant leaves the first and third addresses unchanged; all three slots are legible from the entrance.
changes: Reveal the three skulls and their numbered places from the entrance. Leave a visible empty place when one falls.

stages.title: Colour
stages.operation: An impact leaves a colour.
stages.world: Colour enters the forms and disco grid; the skulls remain black and white.
stages.catalyst: Hits still shrink and turn a tile, now also colouring that same tile.
stages.counterpart: Coloured balls and trails; a hostile ground impact colours its local receiver.
stages.reuse: Current per-tile marks and individual materials, plus the existing biome paint texture for later terrain.
stages.next_work: Carry the colour record by surface address when flat tiles later become a height field.
stages.acceptance: Only the actual receiver is coloured. REST retains the mark; RESET restores the declared baseline.
changes: Carry floor colours into later terrain, together with tile scaling and rotation.

stages.title: Tiling
stages.operation: One impact changes a repeated address.
stages.world: A 2 by 2 motif repeats across the 6 by 12 floor. The same shelters and route remain.
stages.catalyst: A hit repeats scale, turn and colour on 18 matching tiles. Any copy can edit that motif address.
stages.counterpart: Its ground marks stay local, distinguishing a local event from the player's repeated rule.
stages.reuse: Current modulo address mapping and per-address hit counts; inherited banner patterns are an optional later surface receiver.
stages.next_work: Fix the reported post-hit console obstruction, then flash all responding copies briefly so repetition reads from standing height.
stages.acceptance: One shot changes exactly 18 copies; four motif addresses remain independent. All 13 controls stay reachable after the shot.
changes: Keep the console reachable after tiles turn and shrink.
Flash all matching pattern tiles together when one is hit.

stages.title: Change
stages.operation: A local rate accumulates into a path.
stages.world: The existing turned tiles can supply a bounded direction field, with arrows sampling the very same rule as the moving ball.
stages.catalyst: Edit the field using inherited tile hits; launch a ball whose position advances by sampled direction times speed times elapsed seconds.
stages.counterpart: Its balls sample the same field. Earlier cover still blocks contact, but a path may curve around it.
stages.reuse: The Flow_Field hall's shared-sampler and trail pattern; current tile turns and hit records. This adapts Claude's floor-steers proposal to the hall's prescribed-velocity subject.
stages.next_work: Build one field adapter and one projectile motion hook. Keep an untouched field straight and a fixed refuge; acceleration and mass enter in Forces.
stages.acceptance: Identical start, field, speed and duration reproduce a path within tolerance. One step and two half-steps are compared. Arrows and projectiles read the same sampler.
changes: Let a shot change the local direction field. The same arrows guide moving balls.

stages.title: Forces
stages.operation: A push changes carried velocity.
stages.world: Add one movable barrier or receiver beside fixed refuge. Mass and momentum now affect how it responds.
stages.catalyst: A shot imparts an impulse; the body continues after contact and can be pushed back.
stages.counterpart: Its projectiles can push that same receiver, using the same physical rule.
stages.reuse: The existing sphere force lineage and impulse study; shared projectile collision. The legacy force_field layer only draws arrows and is not a force solver.
stages.next_work: Choose one receiver with explicit mass and bounded travel; adapt the existing rigid-body interaction without replacing the player's locomotion.
stages.acceptance: Equal impulses on two declared masses produce different velocity changes; the refuge remains fixed and usable.
changes: Let shots push movable cover. Mass changes how strongly it responds.

stages.title: Form-finding
stages.operation: An update searches for a lower cost.
stages.world: A cover arrangement adjusts toward an explicit objective, with a visible stopping condition.
stages.catalyst: Move an anchor or start point; observe a different settled arrangement.
stages.counterpart: It has to navigate the resulting arrangement; do not give it a second unrelated new ability here.
stages.reuse: descent_landscape_lab has real cost, finite differences and stop reasons. Its display is not a walkable or physical terrain; use its update logic, not an assumed collider.
stages.next_work: Map one small optimisation variable to a barrier pose, preserve a safe path, and distinguish optimisation steps from elapsed physical time.
stages.acceptance: For a declared stable step setting the measured cost decreases; SMALL SLOPE, STEP LIMIT and leaving the allowed domain remain distinguishable.
changes: Let a cover arrangement settle through small steps toward a visible goal.

stages.title: Waves
stages.operation: Periodicity becomes walkable relief.
stages.world: The existing floor becomes a shallow sine surface; landmarks and earlier surface addresses remain identifiable.
stages.catalyst: Earlier transform, paint and motif effects remain available on the shaped surface. A later optional control can change amplitude or phase.
stages.counterpart: Crests interrupt sight lines; optionally phase its movement against the same period after the floor is readable.
stages.reuse: SineSpace builds a height mesh and matching trimesh collision through TopologySpace. Use its actual equation and sampler.
stages.next_work: Adapt the surface to the 12 by 24 arena, shallow enough for locomotion; keep it static initially and fit cover, spawn and controls to sampled height.
stages.acceptance: Ray hits match visible crests and troughs; the route is traversable; motif addresses and colour marks survive the surface change.
changes: Make a shallow sine-wave floor that can be walked on. Keep earlier shot effects.

stages.title: Randomness
stages.operation: A seed chooses independent heights.
stages.world: The floor becomes irregular and harder to walk, within a measured slope and height budget.
stages.catalyst: Keep earlier actions while learning a new route through a reproducible uneven floor.
stages.counterpart: A proposed bounded seeded variation in shot timing can follow; first isolate the floor so difficulty does not change in two unexplained ways.
stages.reuse: RandomSpace already has a seed and distribution laws. Disable animation and retain the same draw record throughout the attempt.
stages.next_work: Build a fixed sampled height field, with a traversable corridor and cover clearances. Reset reuses the seed; reroll must be an explicit different action.
stages.acceptance: Same seed and law reproduce the heights; the field does not resample while walking. The route and all controls remain reachable.
changes: Add uneven, randomly raised ground. Keep the same seed when restarting.

stages.title: Noise
stages.operation: Neighbouring heights become correlated.
stages.world: Compare smoother coherent terrain with the preceding independent random floor using the same footprint and a controlled height range.
stages.catalyst: Earlier marks and motif addresses remain. A later field brush can be added once the terrain comparison is clear.
stages.counterpart: Use the landform as cover. A coherent wandering path is an optional next addition, not needed to establish the floor difference.
stages.reuse: NoiseSpace and the generation-17 biome's sampled ground and ecological placement. Reuse the landscape's placement logic progressively, not its full population at once.
stages.next_work: Configure noise frequency and octaves for demonstrably lower neighbouring height differences; equal height range alone does not guarantee smoothness.
stages.acceptance: With recorded settings, neighbouring differences are lower than the random comparison; renderer, collision and object feet use the same field.
changes: Smooth the abrupt ground into connected hills using noise. Keep the same overall height range.

stages.title: Shaders
stages.operation: One surface rule runs at every sample.
stages.world: Earlier colour and pattern fields become continuous surface responses, with one readable travelling mark or ripple.
stages.catalyst: A hit supplies position, colour and time to the material; it does not secretly change the collider.
stages.counterpart: Its impact is another input to the same material rule.
stages.reuse: Existing shaping and pattern shaders, banner materials and biome paint texture. Shaders is currently missing from biome_vocabulary.json.
stages.next_work: Add a deliberate capability entry and a bounded hit-data adapter to one existing shader. Keep material effects distinct from physical terrain.
stages.acceptance: Known hit inputs produce the intended pixel response while terrain ray hits remain unchanged. No shader-specific feature appears before this stage.
changes: Let impacts create surface ripples and patterns on familiar forms.

stages.title: Cellular automata
stages.operation: A painted cell becomes a changing neighbourhood.
stages.world: The addressed floor can advance a local rule in discrete generations; keep a permanent traversable base underneath.
stages.catalyst: Seed or erase cells, then observe their next generation rather than immediately replacing an entire pattern.
stages.counterpart: Its hits can seed the same rule, making local interventions share consequences.
stages.reuse: Grid2D Game of Life cartridge and the batched ca_surface renderer. The old ca_surface runs several steps during construction only; it is not yet a live arena simulation.
stages.next_work: Separate cell state from draw buffers and use one bounded update clock, with pause, step and reset.
stages.acceptance: A known oscillator alternates correctly without in-place update bias; a shot edits one seed cell; earlier movement and surface actions remain usable.
changes: Let a shot seed cells in the floor. Neighbour rules spread the pattern over time.

stages.title: Fractals
stages.operation: A form repeats at another scale.
stages.world: Use bounded recursive structures as recognisable descendants of earlier cover.
stages.catalyst: Select one branch or depth to unfold; preserve a parent-child record.
stages.counterpart: An optional finite split creates smaller descendants; never unbounded head multiplication.
stages.reuse: fractal_bloom actually builds recursive branching geometry. It needs a collider and interaction budget before it can provide shelter.
stages.next_work: Reuse the recursive builder with depth and instance caps; make selected branches collidable and others visual.
stages.acceptance: Expected child counts and parent IDs hold at each depth; maximum instances are enforced and the exit remains clear.
changes: Build cover that repeats at smaller scales. Limit how many levels can grow.

stages.title: L-systems
stages.operation: A rewritten instruction grows a branch.
stages.world: Earlier line segments become branching structures placed within the existing habitat and clearances.
stages.catalyst: Seed a short grammar or prune a branch; the next bounded rewrite changes the structure.
stages.counterpart: Its route or shelter can grow through the same grammar; a new skin alone does not demonstrate rewriting.
stages.reuse: Existing L-system trees, spawn service and the mature biome's tree placement. Retain earlier sculpture and cover candidates through biome_inheritance.
stages.next_work: Expose one production and its interpreted branch record; attach geometry and collision incrementally within a budget.
stages.acceptance: The produced instruction and branch count match the rule; a retained panel is not replaced when vegetation arrives.
changes: Grow branching structures from a rule. Let shots seed or prune them.

stages.title: Procedural generation
stages.operation: Candidate arrangements meet explicit constraints.
stages.world: Seeded cover and habitat parts form a route under declared adjacency, clearance and occupancy rules.
stages.catalyst: Commit a local choice or regenerate a bounded region while keeping its unaffected neighbours.
stages.counterpart: It occupies the generated route, subject to the same placement constraints.
stages.reuse: The mature biome already retains seed, cells and ecological relationships; inherited_form_clearance checks the space around retained forms.
stages.next_work: Add explicit route constraints and a rejection record; ecological proximity alone does not guarantee playable navigation.
stages.acceptance: A fixed seed reproduces the composition. Rejected candidates state the failed constraint; start, refuge and exit remain connected.
changes: Generate different arrangements from a seed while keeping a walkable route.

stages.title: Soft bodies
stages.operation: An impact changes a body's internal shape.
stages.world: One yielding barrier returns from earlier rigid cover, while a fixed refuge remains.
stages.catalyst: Push or pull the specimen; distinguish elastic recovery from a lasting edit.
stages.counterpart: Its balls deform the same receiver, with contact following the real simulation.
stages.reuse: The existing yielding-cube lesson and spring lattice are candidates. The legacy softbody_flora population is not proof of deformable collision.
stages.next_work: Adapt one tested body, pin its boundary and measure contact cost before enabling multiple deformable objects.
stages.acceptance: A real impact changes vertices and subsequent contact; recovery and reset are measured; rigid cover remains available.
changes: Let cover bend under impact and recover its shape.

stages.title: Isosurfaces
stages.operation: A field edit changes a surface boundary.
stages.world: An earlier solid or terrain patch is reconstructed from a scalar field at a declared threshold.
stages.catalyst: Add or remove field locally through the existing sculpture brush idiom.
stages.counterpart: Later it may edit the same limited patch; first verify the player's operation and escape route.
stages.reuse: The ISO sculpture workshop already binds to the museum's mc_sculpt_vr artifact and retains a field history. Its scene binding needs an arena adapter.
stages.next_work: Reuse field history and meshing through a declared receiver; synchronize collider updates and retain immutable route boundaries.
stages.acceptance: Repeated brush edits produce the recorded field, mesh and collision revision; the player never stands on a visual-only replacement.
changes: Let shots add or remove field material. Update the visible surface and its collision.

stages.title: Boolean surfaces
stages.operation: Two solids define union, intersection or difference.
stages.world: A bounded obstacle can acquire a tunnel, a joined volume or an overlap from explicit operands.
stages.catalyst: Place a sphere operand and choose the operation; preserve both inputs so the change can be read or undone.
stages.counterpart: It uses the resulting opening; attack-driven subtraction is a later option, not needed for the first comparison.
stages.reuse: The current Boolean_Verbs hall compares the same two operands. Reuse that contract rather than labelling an alpha fade as subtraction.
stages.next_work: Select the existing hall's solid builder after inspecting its receiver; bound geometry cost and refresh collision.
stages.acceptance: Difference opens a real passage; disjoint intersection is empty; the same operand record can reproduce or restore the result.
changes: Use the sphere to cut, join or intersect solid obstacles.

stages.title: Swarm intelligence
stages.operation: Neighbours change one another's motion.
stages.world: A small group moves through the retained terrain and cover using local rules.
stages.catalyst: Disturb the group or leave a local attractor, then observe its response.
stages.counterpart: Heads now negotiate neighbours rather than merely occupying indexed slots or prescribed orbits.
stages.reuse: Use the actual boid implementation as a candidate. The old swarm_creatures layer only animates phase-offset orbits.
stages.next_work: Adapt separation, alignment and cohesion to a capped head group; share avoidance and neighbour-query budget.
stages.acceptance: Changing one neighbour changes a focal head's trajectory. Disabling neighbour coupling removes that effect under the same initial state.
changes: Let skulls coordinate through local neighbour rules. Use the catalyst to disturb the group.

stages.title: Graph theory
stages.operation: An edge changes what can reach what.
stages.world: Earlier landmarks become nodes in an explicit traversable or signal network.
stages.catalyst: Connect or disconnect a declared edge; observe the changed route or reachable set.
stages.counterpart: It follows the same graph; a connection can provide a detour rather than simply increase attack power.
stages.reuse: The actual pathfinding artifact is a candidate. graph_connections draws proximity edges only; it does not implement traversal or alter the arena.
stages.next_work: Give edges real receiver semantics, stable node IDs and a route query. Current spine places Graph Theory before Machine Learning.
stages.acceptance: Removing one bridge edge changes the computed reachable set; drawn edges match the graph actually used by movement.
changes: Let changing a connection open or close a route between objects.

stages.title: Machine learning
stages.operation: Measured experience changes a parameter or policy.
stages.world: Keep the same arena for a controlled comparison before and after learning or selection.
stages.catalyst: Provide examples or alter an explicit objective; replay the same test conditions.
stages.counterpart: A recorded policy changes one response, with its training evidence inspectable. More aggression is not the definition of learning.
stages.reuse: The nature system's EvolutionSystem and current ML lessons are candidates. adaptive_behavior's pulsing halo is not a learning implementation.
stages.next_work: Choose one actual learning/selection model, specify data and objective, then expose its changed parameter beside an untrained baseline.
stages.acceptance: A saved update changes held-out behaviour under fixed conditions; resetting learning restores the baseline. A glow alone cannot pass.
changes: Let a skull learn a response from examples. Compare it with an unchanged skull.

stages.title: Foundations crisis
stages.operation: A claim carries the conditions of its test.
stages.world: Return to an earlier apparently reliable arena rule and expose its domain, budget or counterexample.
stages.catalyst: Inspect and challenge one claim through a finite, reproducible encounter.
stages.counterpart: It need not gain another weapon; an unresolved or limited prediction can become the encounter.
stages.reuse: Crisis_Synthesis already carries recorded trials, model identifiers, source hashes and checker results. The old paradox layer is rotating geometry, not a proof of undecidability.
stages.next_work: Select one bounded rule and preserve the evidence record; distinguish failed search from disproven claim and unknown from false.
stages.acceptance: The display never upgrades a bounded search outcome into a universal claim; replay retains model and source identity.
changes: Expose a limit of an earlier rule. Let the player inspect what the rule leaves out.

stages.title: QFEP laboratory
stages.operation: An explicit control reaches an actual receiver.
stages.world: Expose a few measured parameters of the accumulated world without resetting its moving bodies.
stages.catalyst: Use the sphere as a control source; read both requested and received values.
stages.counterpart: Share a parameter that changes a concrete behaviour, keeping its effect observable rather than merely increasing difficulty.
stages.reuse: QFEP Synthesis already maps controls to a SoftBody3D specimen and distinguishes settings from interpretation. tunable_field contains static indicators only.
stages.next_work: Reuse one explicit source-to-receiver mapping, then add telemetry for the actual object. Do not claim the dials measure a universal QFEP quantity.
stages.acceptance: The receiver reports the changed coefficient and retains the same body/state; stopping a modulation does not falsely imply stopping all motion.
changes: Connect the catalyst to a real adjustable system. Show how its response changes.

stages.title: After the foundations
stages.operation: Recompose the world and inspect what the rule excludes.
stages.world: A small authored combination of earlier systems, with an editable route and an account of its choices.
stages.catalyst: Build, connect, protect or transform using capacities already acquired; combat can be optional.
stages.counterpart: A former opponent can become a moving force, collaborator or source in the composition.
stages.reuse: The mature biome's seed and community records, inherited form clearances, and current critical lessons. critical_overlay's tinted dome is not evidence of measured bias.
stages.next_work: Choose one inspectable composition and one exclusion question; retain the source record and alternative instead of switching on every system.
stages.acceptance: A changed rule yields a traceable changed arrangement; earlier object identities and earned capacities remain available; exit and replay stay usable.
changes: Combine earlier abilities into a living biome. Let a former opponent become a source or companion.

changes_note: The changes arrays are the editable working plan. Preserve user edits when regenerating reports. Detailed fields remain background proposals; changes are not evidence of implemented behavior.
